subject: Qualify: interop / SLO playbook + proposed next tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@statera.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Qualify: interop / SLO playbook + proposed next tests

Sarah —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same action items. High level notes from discovery:

- Goal: move from manual model hosting to a managed inference layer with predictable SLOs and easier multi-region failover.
- Primary concerns you raised:
  - Uptime target: 99.95% across API surface (global).
  - Failover requirement: cross-region failover without >30s request disruption and no data leakage.
  - Rate-limits: ~500 req/s per application, with occasional bursts to 1k for 2–5 minutes.
  - Error budget: allowed burn of 0.05% monthly; need clear playbooks for emergency rollbacks.
  - Regulatory: EU data residency for some customers (not in scope for initial pilot).

How Redwood compares to the hyperscalers (high-level):
- AWS Sagemaker Endpoints: mature infra, but typical higher cold-start variability and cost per vCPU/GPU; less built-in KV-prefix caching for LLMs which impacts per-token cost.
- Google Vertex AI: strong multi-region fabric; good autoscaling controls but some customers report opaque retry/failover behaviors under burst traffic.
- Azure OpenAI / Managed endpoints: good SLAs at top tiers but limited control over batching/quantization profiles which matters for edge-case latency/costs.

Redwood differentiators to validate in tests:
- Prefix / KV caching that reduces steady-state token cost without sacrificing p95 latency.
- Continuous batching + adaptive kernel selection to flatten p99 spikes under burst loads.
- Smart routing + automatic variant fallback so we can keep serving within error budgets when a region loses capacity.
- Transparent token-level cost and error-budget reporting (we can run a shared dashboard for the pilot).

Proposed next technical tests (we recommend running these as a short pilot):
1) 48-hour soak at 500 req/s steady with 2x 5-minute 1k bursts (validate p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates).
2) Single-region kill: simulate region outage and validate cross-region failover time and request success rate.
3) Error-budget burn test: inject controlled failures (20% increased error rate for 30m) to validate alerts and automatic fallbacks.
4) Latency tail test: synthetic long-context prompts to exercise KV cache and cold-start behavior for both small and large batch sizes.
5) Rate-limit edgecases: concurrent clients with varied tokens-per-request to observe quota enforcement and retry behavior.

Attachments I shared: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO mapping + measurement plan) and a short canary runbook. I've also included a Drive link to the live dashboard we'll provision for the pilot.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm you want Redwood to run the pilot (we can schedule a kickoff the week of May 11).
- Provide an allowlist of source IPs and preferred test domains.
- Let us know whether the pilot should use a shared dev cluster or a dedicated slot (cost/throughput trade-offs).

I'll loop Marissa and Dev to draft the execution timeline and runbook.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben —

Draft plan (high-level) attached: canary-runbook.md. Summary below:

1) Pre-kickoff (2 business days)
   - IP allowlist check, test account credentials, sample prompt sets (Statera to provide).
   - Provision dedicated slot: suggested config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, 512GB RAM, dedicated network egress to mimic customer env. (Dev to confirm cost).

2) Soak test (48h)
   - Load profile: 500 rps steady, two 5-min spikes to 1k rps on day 1 and day 2.
   - Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-route error rate, token consumption, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate.
   - Success criteria: p95 < 400ms for standard prompts; error rate <0.05% sustained.

3) Region-kill failover (short window)
   - Simulate region out by withdrawing route announcement and enforce downstream drop.
   - Measure time-to-successful-failover (time until 95% of requests succeed again), and any permanent error spike. Goal: <30s disruption for in-flight requests where possible (document exceptions).

4) Error-budget exercise
   - Inject transient failure (return 500 for a controlled subset) and validate automatic fallback to compatible model variant / degraded mode.
   - Verify alerting and on-call runbook triggers.

5) Reporting
   - Provide a consolidated dashboard with token-level cost, per-route SLO burn, and traces for representative failed requests.

Attachments: canary-runbook.md (detailed steps), sample SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx). I’ll produce the one-pager for Sarah tonight.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
